metadata.title: Claude, Applying Brand Guidelines.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude branding a document is general design taste or something more specific, using the applying-brand-guidelines skill's own description as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a brand-guidelines skill is SKILL.md, a spec Claude reads, applies, and validates the same way against whatever document you hand it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (hand the skill a slide deck: same three steps run every time; then the same pipeline runs identically twice, and just as readily against a document outside the scope)

beats.narration_text: You'd guess Claude matches your brand — pattern-picks a vibe. It doesn't. It applies a written spec: read the file, run each step, validate the output. Let's take that spec apart.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I get Claude to match our brand?', hesitates on 'match', corrects to 'apply', lands the real question

props.text:
How do I get Claude
to match our brand?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('match' -> 'apply') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening. The applying-brand-guidelines folder holds four files: apply_brand.py, validate_brand.py, REFERENCE.md, and a four-kilobyte SKILL.md carrying the entire instruction set in plain language — no hidden logic, no learned taste. Claude reads SKILL.md, then acts. The file is the program; the model is just the interpreter.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder opening to four files, SKILL.md highlighted; 'not trained on it' callout; 'the file is the program' closer

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens into four file rows: apply_brand.py (14k), validate_brand.py (10k), REFERENCE.md (3k), and SKILL.md (4k) — SKILL.md recolors teal and grows slightly. A 'not trained on it' tag crosses out a brain glyph. Closing line: 'the file is the program'.

beats.narration_text: The instructions live in a Steps section: read SKILL.md, execute each step in order, return the result. Linear by design — no branching unless a step explicitly says branch. That constraint is the whole point. Watch the anchor. Hand it a slide deck: it reads the deck, applies your colors and fonts, hands back a branded deck. Three steps, every time — the same three.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — three linear pipeline phases, then a slide deck arrowing through apply_brand.py to a branded-deck output

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a slide deck, three steps
production_viz.mechanic: Three phase cards appear left to right and connect with arrows: 'read SKILL.md' / 'execute' / 'return result'. They fade back. THE ANCHOR. A card labelled 'slide deck' arrows into a card labelled 'apply_brand.py', which arrows into a card labelled 'branded deck'. Closing line beneath: 'same three steps, every time'. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The anchor returns. Hand it the same deck twice — apply_brand.py returns identical branding both times. That's the payoff of a file being the program: deterministic behavior, not model judgment. Now the reverse. The stated scope is external communications only, but hand it a document outside that scope and the same three steps still run against material SKILL.md never named. validate_brand.py is the check — wrong colors, wrong fonts, wrong scope, all caught the same way. It optimized for repeatability at the expense of range.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same pipeline firing identically twice, then split: identical deck twice = identical branding; document outside scope = same steps still run, both checked by validate_brand.py

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input, same output; then the limit
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 PIPELINE RETURNS, identical, running twice in a row — two matching 'branded deck' cards appear side by side, labelled 'same input, same output'. Then it splits: left card 'in-scope document' → pipeline → clean branding, labelled 'the payoff'; right card 'out-of-scope document' → the same pipeline → branding applied anyway, labelled 'the limit'. Beneath both, a small 'validate_brand.py' tag with a check and a cross — wrong colors, wrong fonts, wrong scope. Closing line: 'only what SKILL.md names'.

beats.narration_text: Applying brand guidelines isn't Claude developing taste. It's SKILL.md — a spec Claude reads, applies, and validates the same way against whatever document you hand it. The model doesn't decide; the file does.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: I want to apply brand guidelines to my team's documents. Read the applying-brand-guidelines skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That walk-through is the diagnostic — it surfaces which steps SKILL.md actually names, and where the stated scope stops, before any pixels move. Go deeper: hand it a document the skill wasn't written for, and ask what changes. Liam, in for Bear.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to apply brand guidelines to my team's documents. Read the applying-brand-guidelines skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it — which steps SKILL.md names, which files apply_brand.py and validate_brand.py are about to touch, and where the stated scope (external communications only) ends.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: hand it a document outside the applying-brand-guidelines skill's stated scope — an internal doc instead of external communications — and ask which steps change and which don't. What does that tell you about the limit of the spec?
